title: Prod go-live authority matrix and evidence automation guide
content:
Purpose:
This document consolidates the authority matrix, automated evidence capture steps, and SIEM/export verification checks required for a production go-live at Redwood Inference. It is written for release owners, on-call SREs, security reviewers, and the release manager.

Scope:
- Applies to hosted and dedicated deployments that will be exposed to production traffic.
- Focus areas: RBAC v2 role mappings for deploy-time operations, audit-log schema conformance, SIEM export/transforms, and automated evidence collection for signoff.

Quick summary (1-line):
Ensure RBAC v2 entitlements are correct for the release, audit logs are emitted and parsable by our SIEM pipeline, and an automated evidence bundle is produced for the release signoff step.

Pre-release prerequisites (owner: release manager):
- Feature branch merged and infra PR approved (link to PR).
- Canary plan and rollback thresholds defined in the release doc.
- RBAC v2 role mapping PR created and applied to staging.
- SIEM export connector configured for staging and validated.
- Evidence automation job exists in CI and runs without errors.

RBAC v2 verification checklist (owner: sec-eng):
[ ] Confirm least-privilege mapping: list of runtime roles -> permission sets attached (deploy, rollback, secrets-read, metrics-read).
[ ] Validate canary operator role cannot escalate to global-admin (run escalation test script).
[ ] Ensure service accounts used by the deployment have key rotation on file and KMS integration.
[ ] Confirm RBAC audit events are emitted for role grant/revoke in staging.

Audit log schema checks (owner: observability):
- Required fields (must exist and be populated in each event): timestamp_iso8601, request_id, actor_id, actor_type, action, target_id, target_type, outcome (success|failure), metadata.json_patch (nullable), region, model_version
- Mutable fields: metadata must not contain PII.
- Retention: raw audit logs retained 90d; transformed SIEM indexes retained 365d.
- Verify sample events: provide 3 example events from staging and confirm parsers accept them.

SIEM export / transform verification (owner: sec-ops):
[ ] Export connector (kinesis -> SIEM) healthy and backlog < 5 minutes.
[ ] Transform lambda mapping matches audit schema; run unit tests for 100% coverage on schema transforms.
[ ] Tagging: add release_id and env tags to every exported event.
[ ] Alert smoke-tests: simulate 401/403 and ensure SIEM alert triggers in < 10m.

Evidence automation (owner: release-automation):
Automated bundle must be produced by the pipeline when the release job runs. Bundle contents (automatically zipped):
- RBAC snapshot (roles.json) showing role->permission mapping at time of deploy
- Audit log snippets (events.jsonl) covering the last 24h and the deployment window
- SIEM connector health report (siem-health.txt) with offsets and latencies
- Signed manifest file (manifest.sig) referencing S3 object keys and CI build id
- Release policy checklist (policy.md) with checkboxes and approver names

Signoff template (required approvers below must sign via the release console):
- Release Owner: verifies functionality and rollback plan (name, timestamp)
- Security Reviewer: confirms RBAC mapping and evidence bundle (name, timestamp)
- Observability Owner: ensures logs/metrics/alerts are green (name, timestamp)
- Product Manager: business signoff (name, timestamp)

Exception approval matrix (for deviations from checklist):
- Low risk (non-sensitive config, short-lived): TL sec + release owner approval.
- Medium risk (privilege expansion for one service, temporary): Sec Eng lead + Head of Infra signoff + mitigation plan logged.
- High risk (new global permissions, PII-related): CISO signoff + exec sponsor + documented compensating controls and timeline.
Steps for exception path:
1) Create ticket (SEC-EXC-xxxx) with reason, scope, TTL, rollback plan.
2) Attach automated evidence bundle.
3) Run tabletop mitigation and attach notes.
4) Secure approval signatures in release console.

Post-go-live monitoring and rollback triggers (owner: SRE on-call):
- Critical alert rate increase > 3x baseline for 5m -> engage runbook and consider rollback to previous model build.
- Error ratio (5xx/requests) > 1% sustained for 10m -> pause rollout and escalate.
- SIEM alerts for privilege escalation events -> immediate investigate and possible rollback.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Can we add a lightweight signed attestation for RBAC snapshots (PKI-based) to avoid manual approvals? (ask: SEC-R&D)
- Should evidence bundles be replicated to a cold S3 bucket for 7 years for audit readiness? cost analysis pending.

Appendix: quick commands and test scripts (links)
- rbac-test.sh -> runs role escalation matrix in staging
- audit-sample-extract.py -> pulls n events and validates schema
- siem-smoke.yml -> CI job to simulate alert path

References:
- Confluence: SEC/Prod-Go-Live-Checklist
- Jira: SEC-4821 (RBAC v2 rollout)
- Infra PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/912

Notes to reviewers: This doc is intentionally procedural — if you prefer a shorter checklist-only variant we can copy this to a one-pager and attach it to the release template.

Document history:
- 2025-09-12: initial draft (Leah Kim)
- 2025-09-26: added SIEM export tests and exception matrix (Marco Ruiz)
- 2025-10-01: updated retention guidance and signoff template (Priya Desai)
